questions.question: Flowerless plants, naked seeds, needle like leaves and cones as reproductive structure are the characteristics of:
questions.solution:
Gymnosperms are characterized by having naked seeds (not enclosed in fruit), needle-like leaves, and cones as reproductive structures.
  • The word comes from Greek gymnos (naked) and sperma (seed).
  • Common examples include Pine, Cycas, and Cedrus.
  • Unlike Angiosperms, they do not produce flowers.

questions.question: Which of the following items has a high fibre content?
questions.solution:
Whole grains have a high fibre content compared to refined grains or animal products.
  • Dietary fibre is found in the outer layer (bran) of grains like oats, brown rice, and whole wheat.
  • Fibre is essential for digestive health and helps in regulating blood sugar levels.

questions.question: Select the correct statement about climax community.
questions.option_1: It consist of only plant population that makes a new ecological system.
questions.option_2: It is an ecological community in which populations of plants or animals remain stable and exist in balance with each other and their environment.
questions.option_3: It is a very first community of ecosystem.
questions.option_4: It is an ecological community in which populations of plants or animals, which are very unstable and exist for very few time.
questions.solution:
A climax community is the final stage of ecological succession where the population of plants and animals remains stable and in balance with the environment.
  • It remains unchanged as long as the environment remains stable.
  • The species composition is determined by the regional climate.

questions.question: In which of the following animals are the stinging capsules located around the mouth and on the tentacles?
questions.solution:
Adamsia (Sea Anemone) belongs to the phylum Cnidaria, which is known for having stinging capsules called nematocysts.
  • These capsules are located on the tentacles and around the mouth to paralyze prey and for defense.
  • Ascaris, Nereis, and Taenia do not possess these specialized stinging cells.

questions.question: In the context of movement of cells, exocytosis is the process by which:
questions.option_1: cell death is brought about through a heavily regulated sequence of events
questions.option_2: a cell takes in the fluids along with dissolved small molecules
questions.option_3: cells move waste materials from within the cell into the extracellular fluid
questions.option_4: cells absorb external material by engulfing it with the cell membrane
questions.solution:
Exocytosis is the process by which cells move waste materials or secretory products from the cytoplasm into the extracellular fluid.
  • It involves the fusion of a vesicle membrane with the plasma membrane to release the contents outside.
  • Note: The opposite process (taking material in) is called Endocytosis.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement about Agar.
questions.option_1: It is used in preparations of ice-creams and jellies.
questions.option_2: Agar is used to grow microbes.
questions.option_3: Agar, one of the commercial products obtained from red algae, gelidium and gracilaria.
questions.option_4: It is used as nutrient and source of fat of bacterial culture.
questions.solution:
The incorrect statement is that Agar is used as a 'source of fat'; Agar is actually a carbohydrate (polysaccharide).
  • It is derived from red algae (Gelidium and Gracilaria).
  • It is widely used to solidify microbial culture media because most bacteria cannot digest it.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
questions.solution:
The pair 'Nucleolus – Synthesis of DNA' is incorrectly matched.
  • The Nucleolus is primarily responsible for the synthesis of Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and the assembly of ribosome subunits.
  • DNA synthesis (replication) occurs throughout the nucleoplasm, not specifically in the nucleolus.

questions.question: Identify the INCORRECT pair of cell shape types and their examples.
questions.solution:
The pair 'Oblong – Nerve cells' is incorrect.
  • Nerve cells (neurons) are typically long and branched to facilitate the transmission of electrical impulses over distances.
  • Muscle cells are elongated/spindle-shaped, and Amoeba is irregular due to pseudopodia.

questions.question: Which of the following was discovered by GN Ramachandran?
questions.option_2: Fluid mosaic model of a cell
questions.solution:
G.N. Ramachandran is famous for discovering the triple helical structure of collagen.
  • He also developed the 'Ramachandran Plot' to understand the allowed conformations of peptide chains.
  • His work was fundamental to the field of structural biology.

questions.question: ________is associated with the production and metabolism of fats and steroid hormones.
questions.solution:
The Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER) is the primary site for the production and metabolism of fats (lipids) and steroid hormones.
  • Unlike the Rough ER, the SER lacks ribosomes and is involved in detoxification and calcium storage.

questions.question: The dry cell is made up of an outer __________ container that acts as the anode.
questions.solution:
In a dry cell (Leclanché cell), the outer zinc container acts as the anode (negative terminal).
  • The cathode is typically a carbon (graphite) rod surrounded by manganese dioxide and carbon powder.

questions.question: ________ is the study of the distribution and movement of water both on and below the Earth’s surface, as well as the impact of human activity on water availability and conditions.
questions.solution:
Hydrology is the scientific study of the distribution, movement, and properties of water on Earth and in the atmosphere.
  • It encompasses the water cycle and the impact of human activity on water resources.

questions.question: AIDS is an abbreviation for:
questions.solution:
AIDS stands for Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome.
  • It is a chronic, potentially life-threatening condition caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV).

questions.question: Chromosomes found in the salivary glands of Drosophila are:
questions.solution:
The salivary glands of Drosophila (fruit fly) contain polytene chromosomes, which are giant chromosomes.
  • These form through repeated rounds of DNA replication without cell division (endomitosis).
  • They are used by researchers to study gene expression and chromosome structure.

questions.question: What is the root-like structure at the base of an algae (seaweed) that binds the algae to a hard substrate like a stone?
questions.solution:
A Holdfast is the root-like structure at the base of algae that anchors it to a substrate like a rock.
  • Unlike true roots, the holdfast does not absorb nutrients; its primary function is strictly attachment.

questions.question: What are ribosomes made up of?
questions.solution:
Ribosomes are composed of Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins.
  • They are the sites of protein synthesis (translation) in all living cells.

questions.question: Which glands help in digestion in the stomach?
questions.solution:
Gastric glands located in the lining of the stomach secrete digestive juices including hydrochloric acid and the enzyme pepsin.
  • These secretions are essential for breaking down proteins and killing harmful bacteria.

questions.question: Rickets is caused by deficiency of:
questions.solution:
Rickets is a skeletal disorder caused by a deficiency of Vitamin D, calcium, or phosphate.
  • It leads to softening and weakening of the bones in children, often resulting in bowed legs.

questions.question: Which of the following bacteria grow in milk and convert it to curd?
questions.solution:
Lactic Acid Bacteria (LAB), such as Lactobacillus, grow in milk and convert it into curd.
  • During this process, LAB produce acids that coagulate the milk proteins and increase the Vitamin B12 content.

questions.question: In 1955, who published a comprehensive study of small particle constituents of the cytoplasm' (ribosomes) and correctly estimated their physiological importance?
questions.solution:
George E. Palade was the scientist who published a comprehensive study of ribosomes in 1955.
  • He was awarded the Nobel Prize for his work in characterizing these 'small particle constituents' of the cytoplasm.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a vertebrate?
questions.solution:
Mammals are an example of vertebrates because they possess a backbone (vertebral column).
  • Crustaceans, Insects, and Molluscs are all invertebrates.

questions.question: A plant cell wall is mainly composed of:
questions.solution:
A plant cell wall is mainly composed of cellulose.
  • Cellulose is a complex polysaccharide that provides structural support and protection to the plant cell.

questions.question: Which type of muscles do the uterus, iris of the eye, and bronchi contain?
questions.solution:
The uterus, iris of the eye, and bronchi contain smooth muscles.
  • Smooth muscles are involuntary and non-striated, controlling the movement of internal organs.

questions.question: What is called the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.solution:
Mitochondria are known as the powerhouse of the cell.
  • They generate most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), used as a source of chemical energy.

questions.question: Which of the following classes has the largest number of animals?
questions.solution:
The class Insecta (Insects) contains the largest number of animal species on Earth.
  • They belong to the phylum Arthropoda and represent more than half of all living organisms.

questions.question: Which chromosome is involved in the production of ‘masked’ mRNAs for early development?
questions.solution:
Lampbrush chromosomes are involved in the production of 'masked' mRNAs.
  • These are giant chromosomes found in the oocytes (immature eggs) of many animals, where high levels of gene transcription occur to prepare for early embryonic development.

questions.question: On which of the following component of chloroplast is chlorophyll arranged?
questions.solution:
Chlorophyll is arranged on the thylakoids within the chloroplast.
  • The thylakoids are membrane-bound compartments where the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis take place.

questions.question: Foods like pizza, burger are rich in:
questions.solution:
Fast foods like pizza and burgers are typically high in carbohydrates and fats.
  • While they contain some protein, they are often considered 'calorie-dense' due to the refined flour and high sugar/fat content.

questions.question: Which vitamin prevents the neural tube defect in new-born babies?
questions.solution:
Folic acid (Vitamin B9) is crucial for pregnant women to prevent neural tube defects (like spina bifida) in newborns.
  • It helps in the proper development of the baby's brain and spinal cord.

questions.question: The disease caused by deficiency of iodine is:
questions.solution:
A deficiency of iodine in the diet leads to goitre.
  • Iodine is required by the thyroid gland to produce hormones; its absence causes the gland to enlarge, creating a swelling in the neck.

questions.question: ______ is found in the cell wall of Spirogyra.
questions.solution:
The cell wall of Spirogyra is made up of cellulose.
  • Spirogyra is a green algae, and like land plants, its structural support comes primarily from cellulose and pectin.

questions.question: How can biotic potential be defined?
questions.option_1: The maximum number of offspring of a species that can survive but cannot reproduce
questions.option_2: The maximum number of offspring that can be produced by a species
questions.option_3: The minimum number of offspring that can be produced by a species
questions.option_4: The maximum number of offspring of a species that cannot survive after birth
questions.solution:
Biotic potential is the maximum number of offspring that could be produced by a species under ideal environmental conditions.
  • It represents the unrestricted growth rate of a population.

questions.question: Which of the following cell organelles is involved in apoptosis?
questions.solution:
Mitochondria play a central role in apoptosis (programmed cell death).
  • They release signaling proteins like Cytochrome c into the cytoplasm, which triggers the cascade of events leading to the cell's self-destruction.
